back: An organisational entity placed under the authority of a manager who has been delegated (more or less) decision-making power and given performance targets.
A system for measuring the performance of an organisation's responsibility centres from a financial perspective. Part of management reporting.

Can act on costs, but not on revenues or assets.
→ cost indicator

Can act on revenues, but not on the cost of products & services sold, nor on assets.
→ revenue indicator

Can act on costs and revenues, but not on assets.
→ profitability indicator

Can act on costs, revenues and assets.
→ return on investment indicator
A responsibility centre's span of accountability should be adjusted to its span of control.
The performance indicators used to set objectives and evaluate the results of a responsibility centre.
The extent to which a responsibility centre can control the performance dimensions of its activity (costs, revenues, assets …).

Top management: clarify the expected contribution of each centre and assess its performance.
Local managers: identify the boundaries of their responsibility and guide operational actions.
Too coarse for real decision power; controllability often partial; hybrid centres exist → adjust the "typical" indicator, tailor-made approach.
